How have you gone about learning to program?

I'm forced to learn it because of my major. I have to learn Verilog/VDHL, C/C++, and MATLAB.
But, for the fun of it, I tried learning HTML basic when I was younger just by trial and error on notepad and using a hosting site to see if it works, then again, I was really programming in CSS from looking at snippets. Of course, I forget most of that because Geocities died... THANKS YAHOO!!!

I jumped into python completed the code academy course but I feel like it didn't tech very much accept very basic stuff. There's very little I can do with what I learned and it's discouraged me from learning other code excluding hrml5 and css.
Read a book. Books are always much more informative and they dig much deeper into the language.

A good learning tool I used was html5 canvas and building a game with it. I made a simple racing game.

It'll give you exposure to html, css, jquery, and javascript. You'll have many questions on how things work, when you find something you don't know about, look it up, read about it or watch a video, go back to your game and implement your learning.

Building games with canvas is fun because it gives you something tangible that you can play and experiment with. I personally found it an enjoyable experience that taught me quite a bit about programming.

I've been using Free Code Camp. It's the first resource I've come across that is linear. As someone with ADHD, I often got distracted on sites like Codecademy with so many different options. I would start one course, not finish it, then move on to another. I tried learning way to many languages at once rather than trying to learn the underlying concepts. While Free Code Camp focuses on web development, their methods are sound. Don't spread yourself too thin and try to obtain a good foundation. Choose one language to start with and stay focused.

Just a little disclaimer: I am just a self-taught hobbyist programmer that's been dabbling for a couple of years in Python. Recently (as in the last few days) been trying to learn C. Just figured pointers out the other day (It's a pretty simple concept once you get it). Was a good day. Still don't fully grasp memory management, but I'll get to it.

Anyway, I tend to use written tutorials, and books more than anything else. Videos are great, but I always end up back at written material. There's just more of it, and I find that it tends to be more informative than most videos.

I also learn by just experimenting. Writing dumb little scripts that do nothing useful. Wrote a function in C the other day for splitting a string into words, and then another function for getting a "slice" from the split words (as well as a few other little bits).

And I just want to say that, coming from Python, working with strings in C is a bit of a pain in the ass. But I'm enjoying it, and starting to grasp some of the concepts of C.
I came from C to Python and I feel you.

I have to say that I really like Python. Sure, it's relatively slow, but for most tasks it's fast enough, and writing it is like writing pseudocode. I would highly recommend Python to any beginner programmers -- not that it's only for beginners, because it's not.

I am enjoying learning a bit of C though, because it's a step lower than Python. I like the idea of interacting a little more closely with my machine. It's not assembly, or machine code, but it's a step closer. I wouldn't mind toying with assembly as well though at some point. But that's probably too low to be useful to me. It would just be fun to play with. I have always thought it would be awesome to build a little homebrew computer, based around a little 8-bit CPU (such as the 6502, or Z80), like the homebrew computers that were popular in the 70s. That is probably over my head though. I just like the idea.

Also, because Python is built on top of C (at least CPython is, which is what I'm using), I'll be able write C code that I can use in Python, if I ever need/want to.
Yea I'm really enjoying it and I can't wait to test it out in some cool projects. Best of luck to you!
